title: Traefik CRDs on the removed traefik.containo.us API group
quote: In v3, the Kubernetes CRDs API Group `traefik.containo.us` has been removed. Please use the API Group `traefik.io` instead.
remediation: Re-apply every listed object under the `traefik.io` API group before upgrading Traefik to v3. Traefik v3 does not serve `traefik.containo.us`, so any object left on it stops routing traffic the moment the new version starts. Install the v3 CRDs and update the RBAC to cover `traefik.io` first, then migrate the objects.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.containo.us,ingressroutetcps.traefik.containo.us,middlewares.traefik.containo.us -A 2>/dev/null # any rows = objects still on the removed API group; no output (or a NotFound error) = nothing left to migrate

title: Content-Type is no longer auto-detected

detection.reason: this is request-time behaviour, not a property of any collected object

quote: In v3, the `Content-Type` header is not auto-detected anymore when it is not set by the backend. One should use the `ContentType` middleware to enable the `Content-Type` header value auto-detection.
remediation: Identify backends that rely on Traefik guessing their Content-Type and attach the `ContentType` middleware to those routers. Otherwise responses reach clients without the header, and browsers fall back to sniffing or refuse to render — a change that shows up as broken pages rather than as an error in Traefik.
verifyCommand: kubectl get middlewares.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.contentType != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed re-enable auto-detection for the routers that reference them; nothing printed means no backend gets a guessed Content-Type in v3

title: A batch of deprecated options is removed in v3

detection.reason: checked in the Traefik workload's container args only (Deployment or DaemonSet) — an option set through a static configuration file or environment variables is not scanned

remediation: Audit the static configuration and middleware definitions for the whole removed set, not just the Datadog tag. Two different failure modes: (1) static options such as `tracing.datadog.globaltag` and `tls.caOptional` on ForwardAuth and the HTTP/Consul/Etcd/Redis/ZooKeeper/Consul Catalog/Docker providers are rejected at startup — a failed rollout; (2) the Headers middleware's `sslRedirect`, `sslTemporaryRedirect`, `sslHost`, `sslForceHost` and `featurePolicy` are still ACCEPTED by the v3 CRD but no longer applied, so the HTTP→HTTPS redirect silently disappears with no error or log — move it to an entry-point redirection or a RedirectScheme middleware before upgrading. StripPrefix `forceSlash` is still honoured, with a deprecation warning.
verifyCommand: kubectl get middlewares.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.headers.sslRedirect // .spec.headers.sslHost // .spec.headers.featurePolicy // .spec.stripPrefix.forceSlash // .spec.forwardAuth.tls.caOptional) != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed still set an option v3 drops (ssl* are ignored silently)

title: experimental.http3 is removed and blocks startup

detection.reason: checked in the Traefik workload's container args only (Deployment or DaemonSet) — an option set through a static configuration file or environment variables is not scanned

quote: In v3, HTTP/3 is no longer an experimental feature. It can be enabled on entry points without the associated `experimental.http3` option, which is now removed.
remediation: Remove `http3` from the `experimental` section and enable HTTP/3 on the entryPoint instead. Traefik refuses to start on the removed option, so leaving it in place turns the upgrade into a CrashLoopBackOff rather than a degraded route.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.args[]? | tostring | test("experimental.http3")) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed will fail to start on v3; also check the Helm values and any static config ConfigMap

title: Gateway API experimental channel resources are off by default

detection.reason: TLSRoute and TCPRoute belong to the Gateway API (gateway.networking.k8s.io), which this add-on's collection does not claim; only IngressRoute, IngressRouteTCP and Middleware are collected

quote: In v3, the Kubernetes Gateway API provider does not enable support for the experimental channel API resources by default.
remediation: If any TLSRoute or TCPRoute is in use, set the `experimentalChannel` option on the Kubernetes Gateway provider before upgrading. Without it those routes are simply not reconciled in v3 — the objects stay in the cluster and look healthy, so the failure shows up as traffic that stops being routed rather than as an error.
verifyCommand: kubectl get tlsroutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io,tcproutes.gateway.networking.k8s.io -A 2>/dev/null # any rows = experimental-channel routes that need experimentalChannel enabled; a NotFound error = the CRDs are absent and this does not apply

title: Kubernetes Ingress default path matching no longer supports regexes

detection.reason: this concerns the path values of Kubernetes Ingress objects and the Traefik annotations on them, neither of which is part of the Traefik CR projection this source evaluates

quote: In v3, the Kubernetes Ingress default path matching does not support regexes anymore.
remediation: Find Ingress paths that rely on regex behaviour and pick one of the two documented remediations: keep v2 interpretation of `PathPrefix` via the install configuration or the `traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.rulesyntax` annotation, or rewrite the path as a Go-syntax regex and select the `PathRegexp` matcher with `traefik.ingress.kubernetes.io/router.pathmatcher`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $i | .spec.rules[]?.http.paths[]? | select(.path | test("[\\[\\]().*+?^$|]")) | $i.metadata.namespace + "/" + $i.metadata.name + "  " + .path' # paths printed contain regex metacharacters and change meaning under v3

title: IPWhiteList middleware is deprecated in favour of IPAllowList

detection.reason: the Middleware projection names each Middleware's types; a MiddlewareTCP is not collected, so a TCP ipWhiteList is not checked

quote: In v3, we renamed the `IPWhiteList` middleware to `IPAllowList` without changing anything to the configuration.
remediation: Rename the middleware type from `ipWhiteList` to `ipAllowList` in every Middleware object; the configuration body is unchanged. Not urgent: v3.0 through v3.7.14 still build `ipWhiteList` as a deprecated middleware (commit ff7966f9c re-introduced it), so routes keep working — the rename only avoids a future removal.
verifyCommand: kubectl get middlewares.traefik.io,middlewares.traefik.containo.us -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.ipWhiteList != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed still use the deprecated ipWhiteList type

title: Per-level open connections metrics replaced by a single global metric

detection.reason: this concerns Traefik's own metrics output, which this platform does not scrape

quote: In v3, the open connections metric has been replaced with a global one because it was erroneously at the HTTP level, and providing misleading information.
remediation: Rebuild any dashboard or alert using `traefik_entrypoint_open_connections`, `traefik_router_open_connections` or `traefik_service_open_connections`. They are replaced by one global metric, so per-entrypoint and per-service breakdowns are no longer available — panels keep rendering while quietly returning nothing.

title: Query(`key=value`) silently never matches in v3

detection.reason: checked spec.routes[].match on IngressRoute for a Query matcher whose single value holds key=value; v3 reads that whole string as the name of a parameter without a value; a router that opts back into the v2 syntax (routes[].syntax: v2) still matches it and is named anyway, because the per-route syntax is not collected; matcher names are matched in any case, as Traefik also registers each one in lower, upper and title case

quote: `Query` can take a single value to match is the query value that has no value (e.g. `/search?mobile`).
remediation: Rewrite ``Query(`key=value`)`` as ``Query(`key`, `value`)`` before upgrading. v3 reads a one-value Query as the name of a query parameter that has no value, so ``Query(`mobile=true`)`` looks for a parameter literally named `mobile=true`: the router is built, nothing is logged, and it never matches, so those requests fall through to another router or get a 404.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]? | select(.match | test("\\b(Query)\\s*\\(\\s*(`[^`]*=|\"[^\"]*=)"; "i")) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  " + .match' # rows printed use the v2 key=value form, which v3 never matches

title: KubernetesCRD RBAC and CRDs must be updated for TCPServersTransport

detection.reason: the agent collects IngressRoute, IngressRouteTCP and Middleware, not the ClusterRole backing Traefik's own service account, so the grant this note is about is outside the collected projection

quote: In v3, the support of `TCPServersTransport` has been introduced. When using the KubernetesCRD provider, it is therefore necessary to update RBAC and CRDs (See requirements).
remediation: Apply the v3 CRD manifests and the matching ClusterRole before upgrading. Traefik reads the new `TCPServersTransport` kind at startup; without the CRD and the RBAC grant it logs permission errors and the KubernetesCRD provider degrades rather than failing loudly.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd tcpserverstransports.traefik.io >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "CRD present" || echo "MISSING tcpserverstransports.traefik.io"; kubectl get clusterrole -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.rules[]?.resources[]? == "tcpserverstransports") | .metadata.name' # a name confirms the RBAC grant exists

title: Router rules must move to the v3 matcher syntax

detection.reason: checked spec.routes[].match on IngressRoute and IngressRouteTCP for the v2-only constructs the v3 syntax drops — Headers()/HeadersRegexp() (renamed Header/HeaderRegexp), HostHeader() (removed) and {name} path placeholders; a rule that parses under both syntaxes but changes meaning is not scanned

quote: In v3, a new rule matchers syntax has been introduced for HTTP and TCP routers. The default rule matchers syntax is now the v3 one, but for backward compatibility this can be configured.
remediation: Audit every router rule for the v2 constructs the v3 syntax renames or drops — `Headers`/`HeadersRegexp` become `Header`/`HeaderRegexp`, and `PathPrefix` no longer accepts a regular expression. Either migrate the expressions, or set the `defaultRuleSyntax` install option (or the per-router rule-syntax annotation) to `v2` to buy time; that fallback is itself deprecated and goes away in the next major version.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io,ingressroutetcps.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]? | select(.match | test("Headers\\(|HeadersRegexp\\(")) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  " + .match' # rows printed use v2-only matchers; also review any PathPrefix that contains a regex

title: Matchers given several values stop building their router in v3

detection.reason: checked spec.routes[].match on IngressRoute and IngressRouteTCP for a one-value matcher (Host, HostRegexp, Path, PathPrefix, PathRegexp, Method, ClientIP, HostSNI, HostSNIRegexp, ALPN) given a second value; a router that opts back into the v2 syntax (routes[].syntax: v2, or the defaultRuleSyntax install option) still accepts it and is named anyway, because the per-route syntax is not collected; matcher names are matched in any case, as Traefik also registers each one in lower, upper and title case

quote: All matchers now take a single value (except `Header`, `HeaderRegexp`, `Query`, and `QueryRegexp` which take two) and should be explicitly combined using logical operators to mimic previous behavior.
remediation: Split every multi-value matcher into single-value matchers joined with `||` before upgrading: ``Host(`a.example.com`, `b.example.com`)`` becomes ``Host(`a.example.com`) || Host(`b.example.com`)``. On v3 Traefik rejects the rule with "unexpected number of parameters" and builds no router for it, so the route answers 404 until it is rewritten. A router that sets `syntax: v2` (or an install with `defaultRuleSyntax=v2`) keeps the old form working, but that fallback is deprecated since v3.4.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io,ingressroutetcps.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]? | select(.match | test("\\b(Host|HostRegexp|Path|PathPrefix|PathRegexp|Method|ClientIP|HostSNI|HostSNIRegexp|ALPN)\\s*\\(\\s*(`[^`]*`|\"[^\"]*\")\\s*,"; "i")) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  " + .match' # rows printed pass a second value to a one-value matcher

title: TCP LoadBalancer terminationDelay moved to TCPServersTransport

detection.reason: the setting lives on a service under spec.routes[].services[], nested inside the routes array rather than at the top level of the projection

quote: The TCP LoadBalancer `terminationDelay` option has been deprecated. This option can now be configured directly on the `TCPServersTransport` level, please take a look at this documentation
remediation: Move `terminationDelay` from the TCP service definition onto a `TCPServersTransport`. The option governs how long Traefik waits before closing a half-open TCP connection, so dropping it silently changes connection teardown for long-lived TCP traffic.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutetcps.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]?.services[]? | select(.terminationDelay != null) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name' # names printed still set the deprecated option on the service

title: Vendor tracing backends stop Traefik v3 from starting

detection.reason: checked in the Traefik workload's container args only (Deployment or DaemonSet) — a tracing backend set through a static configuration file or environment variables is not scanned

quote: Traefik v3 **no** longer supports direct output formats for specific vendors such as Instana, Jaeger, Zipkin, Haystack, Datadog, and Elastic.
remediation: Remove every `--tracing.<vendor>.*` option and `--tracing.spanNameLimit`, and configure `--tracing.otlp.*` instead, pointing at the vendor's OTLP ingestion endpoint or at an OpenTelemetry Collector that exports in the vendor's format. While any of them is set, v3 logs that the tracing backend "has been removed in v3" and refuses to start, so the rollout fails and every route this controller serves goes down.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.template.spec.containers[] | .args[]? | select(test("^-{1,2}tracing\\.(jaeger|zipkin|datadog|instana|haystack|elastic|spanNameLimit)"; "i")) | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name + "  " + .' # args printed stop Traefik v3 at startup
